'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2024 Kursk offensive]]
****[[Russia]] introduces a "[[counter-terrorist]] regime" in [[Belgorod Oblast|Belgorod]], [[Bryansk Oblast|Bryansk]], and [[Kursk Oblast]]s in response to the ongoing incursion, resulting in travel restrictions and an increased security presence. [https://www.novinite.com/articles/227669/Russian+Border+Regions+Under+Counter-Terrorist+Regime+as+Ukraine+Advances (''Novinite'')] [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2024/08/10/7469768/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'')]
****The state-run Russian news agency [[TASS]] reports that over 76,000 residents have evacuated from Kursk Oblast this week. [https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-updates-russia-says-76000-evacuated-from-kursk/live-69906248 (DW)]
****[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] enter Belgorod Oblast for the first time during the ongoing incursion, reportedly capturing the village of [[Poroz]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/ukrainian-forces-entered-another-russian-oblast-media-say/ (''Kyiv Independent'')] 
***The [[Ukrainian Navy]] strikes and heavily damages a Russian offshore [[natural gas]] platform in the [[Black Sea]] being used by the [[Russian Armed Forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-says-it-hit-an-offshore-gas-platform-used-by-russian-forces-2024-08-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[Belarusian involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[President of Belarus]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] increases [[Belarus]]'s defensive presence on the [[Belarus–Ukraine border]] after accusing [[Ukraine]] of illegally sending about a dozen intercepted [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drones]] across the border into Belarusian [[airspace]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/lukashenka-drones-ukraine-claim/33073623.html (RFE/RL)]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***One worker is killed and several others are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[missile strike]] on a "critical infrastructure facility" in [[Kramatorsk]]. [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2024/08/10/7469784/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'')]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Al-Tabaeen school attack]]
***[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] rockets strike Al-Tabaeen school in [[Gaza City]] during [[Fajr prayer|Fajr morning prayers]], killing more than 93 [[Palestinians]] and injuring 47 others, several of whom were trapped in the building as it was damaged by a fire. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/8/10/israels-war-on-gaza-live-70000-flee-new-israeli-operation-in-khan-younis (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-hits-hamas-post-in-gaza-school-used-as-civilian-shelter-group-claims (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Rohingya conflict]]
**Over seventy people are killed in an [[Arakan Army]] [[drone attack]] on [[Rohingya people]] fleeing [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/many-dozens-rohingya-including-children-killed-drone-attack-while-fleeing-2024-08-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Religion and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[President of Ukraine]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] announces [[Government of Ukraine|governmental]] deliberations toward banning a traditionally [[Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)|Russia-linked branch]] of the [[Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)|Orthodox Church]] in Ukraine in order to strengthen the country's "[[Religion in Ukraine|spiritual independence]]". [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraines-zelenskiy-suggests-moves-towards-banning-orthodox-church-with-moscow-2024-08-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Kiteezi Landfill#2024 landfill avalanche|2024 Kiteezi landslide]]
**Eighteen people are killed and fourteen others are rescued after a [[landslide]] at [[Kiteezi Landfill]], a [[Landfill|rubbish dump]] in [[Kampala]], [[Uganda]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/8/11/uganda-garbage-dump-landslide-kills-at-least-12-displaces-many (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement]]
**[[Non-cooperation movement (2024)|Non-cooperation movement]]
***[[Chief Justice of Bangladesh]] [[Obaidul Hassan]] [[resign]]s following an [[ultimatum]] from protesters and is briefly succeeded by [[Md. Ashfaqul Islam]] on an acting basis. [[Syed Refat Ahmed]] is later appointed Chief Justice by [[President of Bangladesh|President]] [[Mohammed Shahabuddin]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bangladesh-hasina-yunus-student-protest-chief-justice-9b3f6070d35e60e5e4bd9b47d9976690 (AP)] [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/354279/ashfaqul-islam-appointed-as-acting-chief-justice (''Dhaka Tribune'')] [https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/bt56y1vfs9 (Prothom Alo English)]
*[[2024 United States presidential election]]
**[[Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign]]
***Officials of the [[Donald Trump]] campaign report that it was hacked by anonymous sources, with the campaign formally blaming "foreign sources", specifically claiming that [[Iran]] was behind the hacking. [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/trump-campaign-says-it-was-hacked-by-foreign-actors/5692955/ (WNBC-TV)]
*[[2024 United Kingdom riots]]
**Thousands of [[anti-racism]] protesters march in cities across the [[United Kingdom]] to protest against [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right]] riots, [[politics of the United Kingdom|political]] figures, and the [[Reform UK]] party. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-thousands-join-anti-racism-rallies-far-right-stays-away/a-69909302 (DW)]
**A petrol bomb is thrown towards an [[Islam in Northern Ireland|Islamic]] centre in [[Newtownards]], [[County Down]], [[Northern Ireland]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c984dzxg6eko (BBC)]
*[[2024 Serbian environmental protests]]
**Tens of thousands of [[environmentalist]] and anti-[[Aleksandar Vučić]] protesters demonstrate in [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]], to protest a [[European Union]]–backed plan to develop [[Europe]]'s [[Jadar mine|largest lithium mine]] in the [[Jadar (Serbia)|Jadar]] valley. [https://apnews.com/article/serbia-lithium-protest-eu-russia-a731e86da3a1aaca0338eba2d629a5cc (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Albania at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Chermen Valiev]] wins a bronze medal in [[Wrestling at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle 74 kg|Men's freestyle 74 kg wrestling]], earning [[Albania]] its [[Albania at the Olympics|first ever]] Olympic medal. [https://www.koha.net/en/paris-2024/428509/historike-medalja-e-pare-olimpike-per-shqiperine (KOHA)]
**[[Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***In the first-ever men's [[breakdancing]] event at the Olympics, [[Philip Kim (breakdancer)|Philip "Phil Wizard" Kim]] of [[Canada at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Canada]] wins the [[Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics – B-Boys|B-Boys]] gold medal, with [[Danis Civil|Danis "Dany Dann" Civil]] of [[France at the 2024 Summer Olympics|France]] winning the silver and [[Victor Montalvo]] of the [[United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics|United States]] winning the bronze. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/breaking/breaking-phil-kim-b-boys-olympics-august-10-1.7290940 (CBC News)]
**[[Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***Three swimmers for [[Germany]] fall ill with [[vomiting]] and [[diarrhea]] and require outpatient treatment after [[open water swimming|swimming]] in the [[Seine]] as part of Olympic competitions. [https://apnews.com/article/2024-olympics-seine-river-illness-02d937f2d5f0fd20efafbf2250264aea (AP)]
**[[Japan at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Rikuto Tamai]] of [[Japan]] wins a silver medal in [[Diving at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's 10 metre platform|Men's 10 metre platform diving]], earning [[Japan at the Summer Olympics|the country]] its first ever Olympic medal in [[Diving at the Summer Olympics|the sport]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/olympics/diving-chinas-cao-yuan-wins-mens-10-metre-platform-gold-2024-08-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[Uzbekistan at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Svetlana Osipova]] of [[Uzbekistan]] wins a silver medal in [[Taekwondo at the 2024 Summer Olympics|taekwondo]] the first ever Olympic medal obtained by a Uzbek female athlete in [[Taekwondo at the Summer Olympics|the sport]]. [https://kun.uz/en/news/2024/08/11/summer-olympics-2024-svetlana-osipova-bags-silver-marking-first-female-taekwondo-medal-for-uzbekistan (Kun.uz)]
